pr_title: Use the current Rails->npm_version for package.json
pr_body:
Fixes #42012.

This takes the [npm_version method from rails/release.rb](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/f95c0b7e96eb36bc3efc0c5beffbb9e84ea664e4/tasks/release.rb#L26-L36) and just copies it.

We probably could refactor this to be DRY but it seems like `release.rb` doesn't call any Rails internals. :thinking:
pr_comments: I haven't tested this yet, and we may want to add a unit test -- but just writing down a PoC while it's fresh in my head

Added test in 46e1b01 but I realized that if someone is using `--main` the version `7.0.0-alpha` is not yet released to npm and setup will probably fail 🤔 

One idea is to just pick `^6.0.0` if the `--main` flag is set 🤔
Doing this, in every Rails release we'll have to remember to change the generator to use the last available version at npm.

@lfalcao Can you explain what you mean?

My assumption was that this will only affect new apps using `$ rails new` and whatever version of version is installed will pin the package.json to use `Rails.version`. The problem I was describing is when that version doesn't have a matching version on npm.
I mean, in the future of `8.0.0-alpha` for example, using '--main' parameter will point to '^6.0.0'. So we'll always have to remember to update this base version.

> I mean, in the future of 8.0.0-alpha for example, using '--main' parameter will point to '^6.0.0'. So we'll always have to remember to update this base version.

yeah or we could just ask `npm` for the latest version and use that 🤔 doesn't npm also support tags like `latest`?

> update: maybe when using '--main' set the github url, then in the other cases use `Rails.version` 👀

Yes - this is what I was thinking too.

I've backpedalled on my idea about the App Updater. Instead I've added details to the upgrade guide. My thinking is:

- For new apps, if we are setting an exact package version in `package.json`, changing this is pretty easy for the user to do. Meanwhile, automating it seems hard.
- We already ask the user to change their Rails version in the `Gemfile`, so this isn't that much more of a stretch.
- We can always fix this in a future PR. The scope of this one is just to fix the [incorrectly loose constraints](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/42012).
Added `thisweekinrails` as I think people will want to know about this when upgrading to 7 (and if you're on 6.1 you should be aware that you should tighten your package.json requirements).
@ghiculescu I went to rebase the CHANGELOG and lost your contribution 😭 Would you mind fixing it? I will see if we can get some more eyes on this. 🙏

issue_context.title: Generated package.json file uses version constraints that may be too loose
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Generate a new rails 6.0 app: `rails _6.0.3.6_ new sample_app`

### Expected behavior

I expected the app to install the `@rails/actioncable`, `@rails/activestorage`, and `@rails/ujs` javascript packages at the corresponding version `6.0.3-6`

### Actual behavior
The app installed the `@rails/actioncable`, `@rails/activestorage`, and `@rails/ujs` javascript packages at version `6.1.3`

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.3.6

**Ruby version**: any supported version

### More information

This happens because the [generated `package.json` file](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v6.0.3.6/railties/lib/rails/generators/rails/app/templates/package.json.tt) declares the dependencies with a loose version constraint:
```json
  "dependencies": {
    "@rails/actioncable": "^6.0.0",
    "@rails/activestorage": "^6.0.0",
    "@rails/ujs": "^6.0.0",
```

(`^6.0.0` will match the latest `6.x.y` version)

I don't think this has really been an issue so far since these packages haven't really had any significant changes. Thus, version 6.1 of the npm packages is likely compatible with a rails 6.0 server. But I wanted to bring this up because I'm not sure this behavior was desired/intentional. I know that rails only expects each framework gem (activerecord, activestorage, etc) to be compatible with the other framework gems of the same exact version, which simplifies maintenance. If that should extend to the npm packages, too, then we probably want to change the generated `package.json` to prevent this behavior.
comments:
Related: [Even in rails 6.1, the generated `package.json` uses `^6.0.0`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v6.1.3.1/railties/lib/rails/generators/rails/app/templates/package.json.tt) rather than `^6.1.0`.

This was a little surprising, since it's declaring that any version >= 6.0.0 and < 7.0.0 is valid - I would have expected the minimum version to be 6.1.0 for rails 6.1 apps. Of course, given that it's a loose version constraint, it does end up installing 6.1.3, so new apps won't actually end up with 6.0.x. Nonetheless, I'm not sure the `^6.0.0` declaration was intentional.

I wonder if we want to do away with the loose version constraint altogether. Would we rather specify an exact version (e.g. by interpolating the rails version)?

> I wonder if we want to do away with the loose version constraint altogether. Would we rather specify an exact version (e.g. by interpolating the rails version)?

This sounds like a better idea. Do you want to make a PR?

We should probably also mention this in the [upgrade guide](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html), or add some smarts about it to the [app updater](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/railties/lib/rails/app_updater.rb).
I was hoping to get feedback/consensus on how to proceed from the core team before opening a PR. I agree that it could warrant updating the upgrade guide and/or `AppUpdater`.

It doesn't seem the `npm` packages are released in sync with gems, so the exact versions may be different. i.e. if it were to map directly to `RAILS_VERSION` that is assuming the npm packages are cut at the same time (which I don't believe they are). I could be wrong though, and this was just a quick look comparing `actioncable` on the npm org and rubygems.org -- so I'd love to find out more.

Hopefully someone can add more context into how these npm packages are published! 🙏

@zzak 
> that is assuming the npm packages are cut at the same time (which I don't believe they are)

I think the npm packages are cut at the same time. See https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/61fb58f6a7f852d765d616d1da41d17851ec7afc/tasks/release.rb#L101-L110

(originally introduced in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/548c1d6e8b819ca4e02e6218b67107c580ee65f2 (https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/24903) to publish the `actioncable` npm package when releasing rails)

It's also part of the release documentation:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/61fb58f6a7f852d765d616d1da41d17851ec7afc/RELEASING_RAILS.md#release-to-rubygems-and-npm

Furthermore, these javascript packages can also be consumed from within the gems themselves via the sprockets asset pipeline. If the npm packages were not cut at the same time as the gems, it would open up the possibility that the javascript in the gem would be out of sync with the javascript in the npm package. That's bad because developers should be able to migrate between the two approaches of javascript consumption freely with the assumption that this won't have any noticeable impact on their compiled javascript.

@rmacklin Thanks for digging in there, and apologizes for my laziness.

I must have not been looking closely (or tired), but it seems that the latest packages exist both on [npm (as 6.1.3-2)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rails/actioncable/v/6.1.3-2) and [rubygems (as 6.1.3.2)](https://rubygems.org/gems/actioncable/versions/6.1.3.2).

Interesting difference in the last version segment on npm vs rg. Though, I'm not sure this matters if we can just use the `npm_tag` when writing to `package.json`.

Still on the table though, is what the team decides is best for version dependencies.

My opinion is that we should leave it open to SemVer (so `^#{npm_tag}`), I think?

> My opinion is that we should leave it open to SemVer (so `^#{npm_tag}`), I think?

I think it should be an exact match, the same as the [Rails gemspec](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/rails.gemspec#L31..L42). Given Rails sometimes makes breaking changes in "minor" (in semver terms) versions, anything else doesn't feel safe.

> I must have not been looking closely (or tired), but it seems that the latest packages exist both on [npm (as 6.1.3-2)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rails/actioncable/v/6.1.3-2) and [rubygems (as 6.1.3.2)](https://rubygems.org/gems/actioncable/versions/6.1.3.2).

I find yarn's website easier to follow than npm's; [here](https://yarnpkg.com/package/@rails/actioncable) the version numbers and release dates seem to match the gem exactly.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/509837/118417683-db831b80-b67a-11eb-9d9b-0a1b202bd3fb.png)

review_comments: Because https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activestorage/package.json isn't a top level file - unlike the `package.json` in https://github.com/turbolinks/turbolinks, or the examples in https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v7/configuring-npm/package-json#git-urls-as-dependencies - I'm not sure how to point a gif ref to it.
`latest` is a bit of a compromise. I imagine someone who knows more about npm than me could make this work.
@ghiculescu While we're here, how about adding tests for the skip options?

I'm not sure if this should be `:nodoc:` or `:doc:` but I guess we don't want to expose it as public API yet?

Also, I wasn't sure if we should add the origin of this method which has a much better description:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/f95c0b7e96eb36bc3efc0c5beffbb9e84ea664e4/tasks/release.rb#L26-L36

Note to self: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/api_documentation_guidelines.html#method-visibility

It seems this whole class is [nodoc'd](https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/Rails/Generators/AppBase.html) so probably adding these comments to the method won't make a difference.
